verdict.rationale: Vercel documents running arbitrary code and libraries on Vercel Functions via the Container Runtime, which uses an OCI image. Its WebSockets docs also say standard npm libraries like ws work with no additional configuration, so serverless functions are not limited to a restricted subset. Coverage is partial because no evidence states that the default Node.js function runtime has full Node API and npm compatibility, and nothing addresses the edge side of the story. missing for 10: explicit documentation of full Node.js API and npm compatibility in the standard functions runtime, evidence about edge functions or middleware runtime restrictions, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run unmodified Node.js code and npm packages in edge/serverless functions instead of a restricted runtime subset

citations.quote: Run any code and library on Vercel Functions with an OCI container image built from a Dockerfile or Containerfile at the project root.
WebSockets in Vercel Functions work exactly like any distributed WebSocket server, so you can use libraries like ws to upgrade connections with no additional configuration
Run server-side code on demand with Fluid compute, which scales concurrency for AI and I/O-heavy workloads.
